title: Kling AI 4.0 suggests a shift in AI video competition from visual quality to directorial control
source_used: TechNode (full text); Pandaily for the preview-to-general-rollout context
key_facts: Kling AI released Kling 4.0, focused on motion performance, creative control and longer-form storytelling (TechNode).
It supports native video of up to 30 seconds in one generation, up to 15 multimodal reference assets (images, video, audio) and up to 10 keyframes (TechNode).
Reference assets guide how a video should look and feel; keyframes let creators define how the story unfolds (TechNode).

A Kling spokesperson told TechNode the biggest bottleneck for longer AI video is stability, controllability and narrative coherence, and that fidelity is becoming a baseline rather than the sole advantage.

TechNode's own assessment: the features could reduce repeated generations, but effectiveness depends on scene complexity, and story development, shot selection and final editing still need human judgment.
Pandaily reports Kling 4.0 moved from preview access to general availability on klingai.com, following a September preview that already announced 30-second clips and multi-reference control.
quote_evidence: Kling 4.0 supports native video generation of up to 30 seconds in a single generation, along with up to 15 multimodal reference assets and 10 keyframes, giving creators more control over characters, scenes, actions and camera movements.
More control does not mean AI can independently make a film.
Kling AI’s latest release, Kling 4.0, introduces features designed to tackle these challenges.
why_it_matters_hint: AI video makers are competing on control and continuity across shots, not only on how real a single clip looks.
event_date: General rollout reported 16 Oct 2026; preview in September 2026
notes: Feature specs are the company's; the analysis (control over realism, effect on repeated generations) is TechNode's. Release date is not stated in the TechNode text; Pandaily's 16 Oct 2026 report describes the full launch. Pandaily lists different reference limits per job (10 images, 5 videos, 7 subjects) than TechNode's 15 assets; the entry uses TechNode's figures.
